title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds automated default profiles for batching/caching and quantization, integrates unit-economics metrics into Optimize UI and CLI. Backwards-compatible; rollout gated by feature flag.
description: Summary: This PR adds a coordinated set of changes to enable automated cost-optimization defaults across the serving stack: 1) autotune default batching and KV-cache policies surfaced in the runtime, 2) model quantization profile selection logic (CPU/GPU-aware) and new profiles for 4bit/8bit targets, and 3) unit-economics tooling integration so Optimize can recommend profiles and expected per-token cost impact. Motivation: customers frequently ask for safe, production-ready defaults that reduce per-token cost without increasing tail latency or regressions in quality. This change implements conservative defaults, an opt-in autotune flow, and telemetry hooks so product/SE can evaluate ROI before broad rollout. Changes included: - runtime/service: autotune controller that suggests batch_size, max_pending, and cache TTL per route based on observed latency distributions and request size histograms. - quantization: profile registry, hardware-aware selection, and compatibility checks (KV cache, attention kernels). - optimize-ui & CLI: new recommendations panel, delta cost estimates, and a 'simulate' mode to preview unit-econ impact. - telemetry: new metrics (uecon_estimated_cost_savings, autotune_suggestion_score), and two new tracing tags for suggestion provenance. - rollout: feature-flagged; default off for existing customers, opt-in toggle in Console; gradual canary to 10% of traffic via rollout policy. Motivation and scope: This is intended as the first phase of the autotune/autorecommend stack. It focuses on defaults and recommendations only (no automatic enforcement). The goal is measurable per-token cost reduction for typical RLHF and chat workloads while preserving 99th percentile latency SLOs. Testing & validation: Unit tests for profile selection, integration tests for the runtime controller using the perf-canary harness, and manual canary runs on dedicated staging clusters. We validated across three representative workloads: short chat (avg 40 tokens), long-form generation (avg 600 tokens), and embedding-heavy batch workloads. Results: conservative autotune recommendations reduced estimated per-token cost by 8-14% with <2% change in 99th latency for chat canary. Checklist: - [x] runtime controller + unit tests - [x] quantization profile registry + tests - [x] Optimize UI integration + CLI simulate mode - [x] telemetry + dashboards - [x] rollout plan with feature flag - [x] docs updated (console docs + quickstart) Migration and compatibility: Changes are backward-compatible. Quant profiles are additive; legacy profiles remain available. Autotune suggestions are advisory by default. Security & perf notes: No new keys or secrets. The quant selection code adds safety checks to avoid unsupported operator paths on older runtimes. Follow-ups: - Phase 2: automatic enforcement under SLO constraints - Phase 3: per-customer default profiles learned from historical traffic - Extend profiles to on-prem edge deployments Commit summary (high level): See commits_summary field for compact commit list.
